en.summary: IPO filing analysis: Anthropic reported rapid Q3 revenue growth but returned to a GAAP operating loss after a profitable Q2. Financing-related fair-value changes dominate the much larger net loss, while the company reports positive adjusted operating income. Evaluate demand, compute economics and long-term capacity commitments separately. ANT is the proposed Nasdaq symbol; this is registration-statement research, not a post-listing earnings release.
findings: The latest reviewed S-1/A reports Q3 revenue of $16.956B, versus $1.382B a year earlier and $11.555B in Q2: approximately 1,126.9% YoY and 46.7% sequential growth. These are recognized quarterly revenues for July 1–September 30, 2026. They must not be substituted with annualized run-rate estimates, customer bookings or IPO valuation headlines.

GAAP operating loss was $567M, versus a $974M operating profit in Q2 and a $3.089B loss a year earlier. Compute and infrastructure expense rose to $9.863B from $5.558B sequentially, while other operating and administrative expense rose to $3.588B from $1.031B. Stronger sales therefore did not preserve Q2 GAAP profitability. Compute expense spans the disclosed operating cost structure and is not a verified cost-of-revenue measure.

Company-adjusted operating income was $2.463B, compared with the GAAP loss of $567M. The quarterly bridge adds back $1.070B of stock compensation and $1.960B of non-cash charitable contributions. This reconciliation explains the difference; it does not make compensation or dilution economically irrelevant. The quarter also had company-adjusted net income of $3.167B, which must remain distinct from GAAP net loss.

GAAP net loss was $23.291B, versus $12.138B a year earlier. A $21.936B fair-value loss on convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs is much larger than the operating loss. It is a financing-related accounting remeasurement, not a dollar-for-dollar statement of cash burned in Q3. Ordinary percentage earnings growth is omitted because both the operating and net-income comparison baselines are losses.

The first nine months produced $6.569B of operating cash flow, alongside $925M of equipment purchases, $1.955B of prepayments for leased assets/equipment and $88M of finance-lease principal. These are cumulative nine-month figures. OCF less equipment purchases alone omits other capacity-related cash requirements. Standalone Q3 cash values remain unfilled here until comparable cumulative periods and classification changes are reconciled.

The filing describes approximately $900.9B of commitments, substantially all tied to compute and infrastructure, including about $70.7B due in the twelve months after September 30, 2026. These future obligations have a different period and scope from current operating expenses or cash flow. Customer demand, utilization, financing availability and dilution must support the capacity build-out; an IPO plan does not guarantee those returns or the final terms of the offering.

segments.name: Consolidated business scope
segments.text: Anthropic reports one operating and reportable segment. Claude product and customer categories are business perspectives, not separately disclosed revenue/profit segments. No unsupported split between consumer subscriptions, enterprise use and API access is constructed in this analysis.

segments.name: Compute economics
segments.text: Q3 compute and infrastructure expense was approximately 58.2% of revenue, versus about 48.1% in Q2, using the disclosed quarterly amounts. This expense-to-revenue ratio helps track capacity costs but is not a GAAP gross margin. Training investment, serving costs and utilization need further disclosure before making a unit-profit claim.

segments.name: Contracted future demand
segments.text: Remaining performance obligations were $13.8B at September 30, with approximately 75% expected to be recognized over the following twelve months. RPO is neither current revenue nor a full measure of future consumption. Compare its contractual scope and timing with capacity commitments without treating the two balances as an immediately comparable coverage ratio.

follow_ups.update: Track quarterly revenue, compute expense and the full operating expense bridge, preserving GAAP and adjusted views.

limitations: This is research on a pre-IPO S-1/A, not a listed-company earnings release. ANT is the proposed Nasdaq ticker; final offering and trading status require subsequent official confirmation.

The quarterly income statement is unaudited. A standalone GAAP gross margin and common-stockholder diluted EPS were not verified and remain null; compute expense is not substituted for cost of revenue.
Standalone cash flow remains unverified; all nine-month amounts in the analysis are labeled cumulative. No unsupported subtraction of mismatched investment classifications is published.
Business perspectives are not additional financial segments; the issuer reports one segment. Non-GAAP reconciliations and future commitments retain their own scopes.
No official earnings-call text or pre-release consensus snapshot was reviewed. Forward commitments and proposed IPO proceeds are not realized revenue or cash.
